root_motivation: A Claude session writes four streams of evidence — pre-compaction memlog snapshots, provfs-attributed file writes, recall memories, and ctrace syscall events — but they live in four separate substrates keyed loosely on session_id. Surfacing 'what happened in *that* session' today is a four-command join. session-postmortem factors that join into one CLI so per-session forensics, self-review playbooks, and Fleet 2 artifacts (letters, zines) can ask the same question once.
user_persona: Joe Yen on wintermute, running Claude Code. Wants `session-postmortem latest` to return a one-page markdown brief of the most recent session for daily review, and `session-postmortem --format json <id>` to feed downstream skills (letter-from-snapshot, conversations-zine). Will use `--brief` from inside /self-review playbooks.

acceptance_criteria.description: cargo build --release green; target/release/session-postmortem --version matches Cargo.toml version

session-postmortem --format markdown <id> against tests/fixtures/session-deadbeef/ produces output matching tests/fixtures/session-deadbeef/golden.md (with env overrides --memlog-dir/--ctrace-dir/recall and provq stub paths pointed at the fixture tree)
--format json produces a single JSON object that validates against schemas/brief.schema.json and round-trips through jq cleanly
--format brief yields <=10 lines, all <=120 columns wide, and contains id, intent, duration, exit, top-line counts
When the ctrace fixture is removed (no ndjson for the session), output includes '## Execve top\n(no data)' rather than panicking or omitting the section
With fixtures for three sessions in tests/fixtures/multi/ where one died unclean, session-postmortem latest resolves to the most-recent by start time; last-died resolves to the unclean one
--out /tmp/p.md writes the brief there with mode 0644 and stdout is empty on success
--exclude ctrace,memlog produces a brief containing only the recall + provfs sections (no Execve, no Pre-compaction headers)

[boot+upstream] With PRDs #1-#4 shipped: a tiny end-to-end test (wrapped subshell touches a file under provfs, writes a recall memory, triggers a synthetic memlog event) produces a session-postmortem latest brief whose four signal sections all have non-empty content
README.md documents subcommands with examples (markdown/json/brief/--out/--exclude); CHANGELOG.md has a v0.1.0 entry

scope: Binary session-postmortem with positional <session-id> and --format markdown|json|brief, --out, --include, --exclude, --ctrace-dir, --memlog-dir, --version

Source: src/main.rs (argv + dispatch), src/resolve.rs (alias->canonical id: current|latest|last-died|prefix|hex), src/sources/{mod,memlog,provfs,recall,ctrace}.rs, src/join.rs (Brief struct), src/render/{markdown,json,brief}.rs

Source resolution: memlog from ~/.claude/memlog/<id>/snap-*.json; provfs via `provq scan ~ --session <id> --format paths`; recall via `recall list --session <id> --format json`; ctrace via `ctrace summary --session-id <id>` (fall back to grepping ndjson under ~/.cache/ctrace/sessions/ if --session-id unsupported)
Mock fixtures under tests/fixtures/{session-deadbeef,multi}/ providing canned outputs for all four sources plus a golden markdown

Env override variables: SESSION_POSTMORTEM_MEMLOG_DIR, SESSION_POSTMORTEM_CTRACE_DIR, SESSION_POSTMORTEM_RECALL_BIN, SESSION_POSTMORTEM_PROVQ_BIN — set during tests to point at stub binaries / fixture dirs
When a signal is absent, emit the section header with '(no data)' rather than dropping it
Deps strictly: clap, serde_json, chrono, which, anyhow (or thiserror). NO tokio, NO async runtime
non_goals: Interactive UI (markdown to stdout, pipe to pager downstream)
Writing a recall memory of the postmortem run itself (PRD §6 open question, leaning no for v0.1)
Owning the ~/brain/postmortems/ path convention — that belongs to a future /postmortem skill that wraps this binary

five_whys_trace.a: Today four substrates (memlog, provfs, recall, ctrace) record per-session evidence in four different shapes. Answering 'what did session X actually do' requires four commands and a manual join.

Self-review playbooks already do ad-hoc joins (cross-session ctrace aggregate, active ndjson inclusion checks). Each playbook re-invents the join. The cost is proportional to the number of consumers, and Fleet 2 (letter-from-snapshot, conversations-zine) will multiply that cost.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a CLI rather than a library?
five_whys_trace.a: Both self-review and the Fleet 2 artifacts shell out — they're either bash playbooks or Rust crates that prefer subprocess to dependency-graph entanglement with the four substrate crates. A CLI is the lowest-friction shared surface. The JSON output mode covers the library-like use case via stdin/stdout.

five_whys_trace.q: Why scaffold ahead of memlog-witness and recall-session-stamp shipping?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD line 11-12 explicitly authorizes this. The join logic is testable against mock fixtures; the only AC that gates on live upstream is AC9. Scaffolding now removes session-postmortem from the critical path of the continuity fleet and lets memlog/recall slot in when ready.

five_whys_trace.q: Why composition (shell out) over invention (in-process readers)?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD §2.4. Each substrate has its own canonical reader (provq, recall, ctrace). Re-implementing them couples session-postmortem to private storage layouts that may change. Shelling out keeps this tool a thin join and pushes substrate evolution to the substrate crates.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does ctrace match session_id when it currently keys by tracer pid?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: PRD §2.3 + §6 open question. v0.1 best-effort: try `ctrace summary --session-id <id>` first; on flag-unknown exit, fall back to grepping ndjson files under ~/.cache/ctrace/sessions/ for the session_id literal. AC9 (the only AC that stresses real ctrace data) accepts either path. A future ctrace PRD may add a first-class index.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should --out create parent directories?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No. --out is 'write to this exact path'; mkdir -p is the caller's job. Matches the principle of not owning path conventions (a /postmortem skill will own ~/brain/postmortems/).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Counter source when the session is dead?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: PRD §2.3. /proc/<pid>/agent_counters for live processes; persisted snapshot via memlog if dead. v0.1 best-effort: read live if any session-pid is still running, else mark counters '(no data)'. The persisted snapshot path is a memlog-witness deliverable; we don't invent it here.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does AC9 gate ship?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No. AC9 is MAY level (live-fleet-after-upstream) so the verified-completed checklist can pair AC1-AC8 + AC10 (9 ACs) against tests and surface AC9 as deferred until memlog-witness and recall-session-stamp ship.
